newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Portucel loss over 1.0 bln esc.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Portucel loss over 1.0 bln esc.

text.p: Portucel Industrial-Empresa Produtora de Celulose, the state-controlled pulp producer, will post a full-year loss of over one billion escudos ($6.6 million) in 1996 and there are question marks over next year's performance, analysts said.
"We see an improvement in 1997, but everything is going to depend on the pulp and paper market, particularly prices," said analyst Pedro Assuncao of Central Investimentos.
Analysts noted that there was no clear picture yet on what was happening to stock levels.

"Yesterday there were reports that Norscan stocks had risen 200,000 tonnes in October and then today another report said growth was only 20,000 tonnes," said Teresa Pinto Leite, an analyst with Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI).
The analyst said that if the rise were only 20,000 tonnes, then there was a chance that prices could recover in the middle of next year.
"If it were 200,000 tonnes, then there is a strong possibility of a further fall in prices," she added.

For Jose Freire, analyst with Espirito Santo Research, some economic recovery in Europe would probably be needed to help prices, given that new pulp and paper manufacturing capacity was coming on stream.

He forecast a loss for Portucel in 1996 of around 1.5 billion escudos while Central Investimentos saw the losses reaching two billion. BPI, on the other hand, was looking for a loss of just 400 million escudos.
Portucel made a consolidated net profit of 18.1 billion escudos in 1995 before world pulp prices subsequently nose-dived. The price stood at 690 ecus per tonne at the end of 1995.
The company put aside 10 percent of profit into a dividend fund which will guarantee shareholders a payout in 1996.
Assuncao saw the company paying 20 escudos, down from 39.9 escudos the previous year.
Portucel has already said it expects a loss in 1996 because market conditions did not allow for a rise in prices in October as once hoped.
The company lost 2.9 billion escudos in the first six months when prices averaged 300 ecus per tonne. They have subsequently recovered to 420 ecus.
The share price, which has been under pressure in recent days, could retreat further if there is no improvement in the outlook for next year, analysts said.
"If they (stock decline) were really 200,000 tonnes, there is room for prices to fall sharply. If the figure were 20,000, they could also fall but in a more moderate way," said Pinto Leite.
The stock was down 0.32 percent at 933 escudos on Friday.
